newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dassault may offer Rafale on lease-source.
newsitem.headline: Dassault may offer Rafale on lease-source.

text.p: Combat plane maker Dassault Aviation is studying ways of financing production of the Rafale fighterbomber and leasing them to the French air force in order to start early deliveries of the planes and sell them abroad, industry sources said.

Cuts in the current six-year defence budget have forced Dassault to examine novel methods of financing the Rafale programme as only two planes have been ordered for 1999, a number it deems insufficient for winning export orders.
One solution being studied is for the firms in the Rafale programme to fund 10 planes and lease them to the air force.
The Rafale Team partners comprising Dassault Aviation, Dassault Electronique, Snecma, Matra and Thomson-CSF could raise bank loans to fund the construction of the 10 or so aircraft.
"These planes could be built before there is an air force budget, which would mean there is need for bridge financing," said an aerospace executive familiar with the talks.

"This would mean a consortium, which could be the Rafale Team GIE partnership, making orders on their own account, as the air force cannot order a plane if the budget does not exist," he said. Rafale Team is a groupement d'interet economique (GIE) partnership formed to market the Rafale abroad.
After the leasing period, the planes would later be sold to the air force when the next six-year budget came up with the necessary funds.

Talks on the deal began in August and nothing has been decided yet, source said. But time is pressing as the financial structure needs to be decided soon so orders can be placed in 1997 for delivery in 1999.
Foreign service chiefs will not seriously consider buying a plane unless it is flying with the national armed forces.
The Rafale is being considered by the United Arab Emirates, along with the F16 Block 60 from Lockheed Martin, as part of an order for 80 long-range, air-superiority planes.
It is also being offered to Norway and South Korea is viewed as an export prospect.
